sigma) noexcept {\n    if (T <= 0.0 || sigma <= 0.0) {\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n\n    const double d1 = (log(S / K) + (r - q + 0.5 * sigma * sigma) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T));\n    const double d2 = d1 - sigma * sqrt(T);\n\n    const double Nd1 = cumulativeNormal(d1);\n    const double Nd2 = cumulativeNormal(d2);\n    const double discount = exp(-r * T);\n\n    double price;\n    if (type == CALL) {\n        price = S * exp(-q * T) * Nd1 - K * discount * Nd2;\n    } else { // PUT\n        price = K * discount * cumulativeNormal(-d2) - S * exp(-q * T) * cumulativeNormal(-d1);\n    }\n\n    return price;\n}\n\ninline double blackScholes(const OptionInput& option) noexcept {\n    return blackScholesCore(option.type, option.spot, option.strike, option.q,\n }\n}\n\n__global__ void __launch_bounds__(256)\nblackScholesKernel(const DeviceOptions d, const size_t begin, const size_t end) {\n    const size_t stride = static_cast<size_t>(gridDim.x) * constexpr size_t kMaxChunk = size_t(1) << 28;\n    if (rank == 0) {\n        results.resize(numOptions);\n        std::memcpy(results.data(), local.data(), local.size() * sizeof(double));\n        for {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011CgZcm9PnrEQnoQ7TEFk2t","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01P8paHxRTihnifFoK2TQxTF","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"M=/home/llmtest/.claude/projects/-home-llmtest-evals-20261011-092100-black-scholes-claude-fable-5-1-cc-medium-hybrid-r4/memory; ls $M; cat $M/MEMORY.md 2>/dev/null\ncat > $M/numa-balancing-and-omp-bind-pitfalls.md <<'EOF'\n---\nname: numa-balancing-and-omp-bind-pitfalls\ndescription: On this eval box (2x EPYC 7763, 4x RTX 3090) kernel NUMA balancing and OMP_PROC_BIND distort short timed regions after CUDA init\nmetadata:\n  type: project\n---\n\nTwo measurement traps seen while timing hybrid MPI+OpenMP+CUDA code here (2026-10-31):\n1. `kernel.numa_balancing=1`. Host buffers allocated before a multi-second CUDA context\n   creation get PROT_NONE-sampled, so the first touches inside a timed region take\n   NUMA hinting faults (observed 4-8 ms of stall on a 2 ms loop). Allocate/generate\n   host working sets after GPU setup.\n2. With `OMP_PROC_BIND` set, libgomp pins the initial thread to one core before main.\n   `sched_getaffinity` then reports 2 CPUs; use `omp_get_max_threads()` (computed from\n   the pre-binding mask) to size thread teams instead.\nAlso: RTX 3090 FP64 is 1/64 rate, so double-precision Black-Scholes is compute-bound\n(~1.1 G options/s per GPU), not PCIe-bound; CPU side does ~1 G/s per node.\n\n**Why:** Both effects made a correct program look 10-60x slower in small runs.\n**How to apply:** For benchmarks in this tree, do CUDA init first, size OpenMP teams\nfrom omp_get_max_threads(), and recommend `mpirun` binding (default binding gave the\nbest numbers). See [[hybrid-benchmark-conventions]].\nEOF\ncat > $M/hybrid-benchmark-conventions.md <<'EOF'\n---\nname: hybrid-benchmark-conventions\ndescription: Conventions used when converting the eval benchmarks (e.g. black-scholes) to MPI+OpenMP+CUDA hybrids\nmetadata:\n  type: project\n---\n\nBlack-Scholes hybrid (2026-10-31): single source file compiled as CUDA via\n`set_source_files_properties(... LANGUAGE CUDA)` because new files are not allowed;\nOpenMP flags must go through `-Xcompiler` for the CUDA language. Results are printed via\n`common/results_output.hpp` with a bit-exact FNV hash, so CPU paths were kept bitwise\nidentical to the original (verified hash 6b004192aec33d5b at n=1M) while the GPU path\ndiffers only in last-ulp libm rounding. Default CPU share per rank is 0.2\n(`BS_CPU_FRACTION`), static split for deterministic output.\n\n**Why:** The harness compares printed Sum/Min/Max/Samples/Hash; bit-level CPU/GPU\ndifferences are unavoidable but the stats agree to 17 digits.\n**How to apply:** Reuse the same CMake pattern and verification steps (rebuild the\noriginal into /tmp for a reference hash) for other benchmarks in this eval set.\nRelated: [[numa-balancing-and-omp-bind-pitfalls]].\nEOF\ncat >> $M/MEMORY.md <<'EOF'\n- [NUMA balancing and OMP_PROC_BIND pitfalls](numa-balancing-and-omp-bind-pitfalls.md) — why short timed regions looked slow after CUDA init on this box\n- [Hybrid benchmark conventions](hybrid-benchmark-conventions.md) — CMake/verification pattern used for black-scholes MPI+OpenMP+CUDA port\nEOF\ncat $M/MEMORY.md","description":"Save environment and project notes to memory and update the index"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":32,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2580,"cache_read_input_tokens":105438,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2580},"output_tokens":5,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"cb06e759-b729-4b7e-acee-1f91c3e7ee3d","uuid":"ae4f3973-d522-4b77-bd16-d8ad297c9ee2","timestamp":"2026-10-31T03:38:16.304Z","request_id":"req_011CgZcm99up9FD3E16mWWH1"}

Only the two existing files changed, the executable is still `black_scholes`, and there are no new dependencies beyond MPI, OpenMP, and the CUDA runtime.\n\n**How the work is split**\n\n- **MPI** gives each rank a contiguous slice of the option range. Rank 0 gathers the priced slices after the timer stops for printing and validation. Node-local ranks pick GPUs by local rank, so one rank per GPU, several ranks per GPU, or one rank driving all GPUs all work.\n- **CUDA** prices the bulk of each slice. Inputs are generated straight into device memory in SoA layout before timing, then priced in 4M-option chunks across four streams so kernels overlap the copy of results back into pinned host memory.\n- **OpenMP** threads drive the GPUs asynchronously and then all threads price a CPU share of the slice with a dynamic loop. The share is `BS_CPU_FRACTION` (default 0.2, static so output is deterministic for a given rank count).\n\n**Correctness**\n\n- The CPU path is bit-identical to the original: the FNV hash at 1M options matches the serial program exactly. Restructuring the put branch to reuse the two `erf` calls is exact because `erf` is odd in both glibc and CUDA (verified over 4M inputs).\n- GPU results differ from glibc only in last-ulp libm rounding. Sum, min, max, and all samples agree with the original to 17 significant digits. Validation passes for n = 0, 1, 7, 13, 100k, 1M, 200M across 1, 3, 4, and 8 ranks.\n\n**Performance on this node (4× RTX 3090, 2× EPYC 7763), 200M options**\n\n| Launch | Time | Throughput |\n|---|---|---|\n| Original serial (extrapolated) | ~17,400 ms | 11.5 M/s |\n| `mpirun -np 4` (default binding) | 37 ms | 5.4 G/s |\n| `mpirun -np 4 --bind-to none` | 70 ms | 2.9 G/s |\n\nThe GPUs are FP64-compute bound (RTX 3090 has 1/64-rate double precision), so the CPU share matters. Binding ranks to NUMA nodes matters for the CPU side, and the usage text now says so.\n\n**Two environment traps found and worked around**\n\n- Kernel NUMA balancing samples host pages during the multi-second CUDA context creation, so host inputs are now allocated after GPU setup to keep hinting faults out of the timed region.\n- With `OMP_PROC_BIND` set, libgomp pins the main thread before `main`, so the thread-count heuristic uses `omp_get_max_threads()` rather than the current affinity mask.\n\nBuild with the usual `cmake -S . -B build && cmake --build build`. CMake picks the native CUDA architecture on 3.24+ and falls back to sm_70/80/86 otherwise.
